extracted.ANSWER_TO_ITEM_6: The $50/month beneficiary copay and the $245/month government/net price are TWO SIDES OF THE SAME PROGRAM - the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge. They are NOT distinct programs, and they are NOT distinct from GATE-BRIDGE. GATE-BRIDGE is that program.

fifty_dollars.who_pays: the Medicare beneficiary at the pharmacy counter

two_hundred_forty_five_dollars.unit: USD per monthly supply, net price to the government
two_hundred_forty_five_dollars.who_pays: this is the net price at which participating MANUFACTURERS supply the drug under the demonstration; it is NOT a consumer-facing price and must never be displayed to a user as what they would pay
two_hundred_forty_five_dollars.located_language: Under the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge, participating manufacturers will provide eligible GLP-1 drugs at a net price of $245 per monthly supply. Medicare beneficiaries will pay a co-pay of just $50 per month.

extracted.DISPLAY_SAFETY_RULE: Because $245 and $50 come from the same program, an engine that surfaced both as if they were alternative consumer prices would be badly misleading. Only $50 is a beneficiary-facing figure for this program.
extracted.trumprx_is_a_DISTINCT_program: TrumpRx.gov is a separate direct-to-consumer cash channel, not the Bridge. Located claim: discounted prices in the direct-to-consumer channel TrumpRx.gov are for drugs commonly purchased outside of insurance, with GLP-1 users without insurance coverage expected to save $3,000 per year. The $50 Bridge copay must not be attributed to TrumpRx, nor TrumpRx pricing to the Bridge.

bridge_parameters_consistent_with_existi.eligible_drugs: Foundayo, Wegovy (injection and tablets), Zepbound (KwikPen) when used to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction
bridge_parameters_consistent_with_existi.indication_gate: the $50 copay applies only when prescribed for a weight management indication
bridge_parameters_consistent_with_existi.outside_part_d: furnished outside the Part D benefit payment flow and coverage; Part D deductible does not apply; no part of the $50 copay counts toward TrOOP; no low-income subsidy (LIS) provided for LIS beneficiaries
bridge_parameters_consistent_with_existi.LIS_WARNING: The absence of LIS means a low-income-subsidy beneficiary could conceivably do WORSE at $50 under the Bridge than under their subsidized Part D benefit. The engine must not assume the Bridge is always the cheapest Medicare option.
bridge_parameters_consistent_with_existi.exclusion: Not all Medicare beneficiaries qualify, including those who already receive GLP-1 medications through existing Medicare prescription drug coverage or are eligible for GLP-1 coverage through the Part D benefit
